fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Aspiring Cop to Undercover Virologist", "body": "Diaz tells Chance Garton that before the lockdown years he was a typical American diet follower headed into law enforcement, and that he stepped away after asking whether he could enforce mandates that clashed with the Christian principles he was raised on. He describes finding Alec Zeck, Amanda Vollmer and Mike Winner and the End of COVID archive he first discussed on InnerVerse episode 94, then five plus years of self-schooling through the Baileys, Kaufman, Cowan and Mike Stone, mentorship under a naturopathic doctor he names as Mary Arch, a naturopathic practitioner certification, the Bigelson academy for blood work, and finally his own practice at terrainuv.com."}, {"title": "Terrain Is Not a Theory, Diaz Argues", "body": "Diaz objects to the phrase terrain theory at all, arguing that terrain simply names everything a person eats, thinks, feels and lives inside, and he contends that symptoms are the body communicating rather than the disease itself. He quotes Harvey Bigelson's line that health is simple and people are complicated. Garton, who works as a biofield tuner, adds the caduceus and the Therapeutae trained at ancient Alexandria as signs that germs now occupy the slot older systems gave demons, and both argue that a medicine split into cardiac, neurological and back specialists mirrors a compartmentalized body rather than a whole one."}, {"title": "The Elevator Pitch Against Germ Theory", "body": "Asked how he opens with a skeptic, Diaz says he asks people how many germs they carry, then claims the body holds roughly ten to a hundred times more germs than blood cells. He points to streptococcus living in every throat and asks why nobody has strep throat daily, likens the gut to soil microbiology that any farmer would recognize, and argues the classical contagion proofs depended on injecting unpurified cultures into the abdomens of guinea pigs rather than on natural exposure. Germs, he contends, are saprophytes eating dead and dying tissue, the pleomorphic microzymes described by Bechamp, Naessens and Enderlein."}, {"title": "Koch, Tuberculin and the Antibiotic Question", "body": "Garton asks why people seem to get better after antibiotics. Diaz calls that reasoning the fallacy of affirming the consequent, then recounts his reading of the history: Robert Koch experimenting with petrochemical dyes, the tuberculin failure that Diaz says killed thousands and got Koch pushed out of Germany, and Bismarck later paying him to blame British ships coming through the Suez Canal. Diaz notes that penicillin is a metabolite of a fungus rather than an anti-germ agent, and contrasts antibiotics with the isopathics Gunther Enderlein set out in Bacterial Cyclology. Garton frames germ fear as a modern version of Plato's noble lie."}, {"title": "Sepsis Statistics and the Cases He Recounts", "body": "Late in the hour Diaz cites roughly 1.7 million United States sepsis cases a year, a twenty to sixty percent false positive range in the literature, and a forty percent false positive rate for the blood cultures called the gold standard, alongside studies from the 1800s and 1900s that he says induced sepsis in animals with no bacteria present. He recounts three client stories as claims about his own practice: a young girl whose pneumonia he says cleared quickly, a woman told she had shingles, and a client with Bell's palsy beside a hearing implant. He closes calling microzymes the chi or prana of the body."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jacob Diaz, aka the Undercover Virologist, joins InnerVerse to bring us up to date on his last five years of research into the truth about germs, bacteria and so-called viruses. Tune in for valuable information that uncomplicates disease, refutes the quantitative particularization of biology, successfully demolishes mainstream germ theory, teaches the purpose and pleomorphic powers of our biome, and brings the cold hard truth to light about what antibiotics do to a body.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"AIDS, HIV, and the Terrain Reframe","body":"Jacob walks through why AIDS is a terrain condition, not a viral infection: it shows up in people who are malnourished, drug dependent, or undergoing chemotherapy, never as a random contagion. He traces how the gay community got blamed in an era of recreational drug use and toxic party culture, and explains why the HIV antibody test is nearly meaningless, since roughly seventy unrelated conditions can trigger a false positive. He shares a client who tested positive, spiraled from the stress of the diagnosis into real symptoms, and improved once the underlying terrain, not a virus, was addressed directly."},{"title":"Biofield Tuning and the Emotional Roots of Gut Health","body":"Jacob credits biofield tuning sessions for teaching him pleomorphism firsthand, describing a client whose lifelong picky eating and digestion problems resolved within a week of a single tuning session, and another whose eczema traced back to unresolved trust issues with his mother, since the mother symbolically represents nourishment. He maps traditional Chinese medicine's organ emotion correlations onto this: kidneys hold fear, the liver holds anger, the lungs hold grief and sadness, and the gut holds trust. Changing the emotional charge, he argues, directly reshapes the gut biome and resolves physical symptoms without supplements."},{"title":"What Holographic Blood Actually Shows","body":"Using a dark field microscope on a single drop of living blood, Jacob shows images that map directly onto a person's physical and emotional history: a broken hand, a hemorrhage later confirmed at the hospital, a liver strained by cord clamping at birth, even a sacrum shaped by childhood sexual trauma. He is explicit that these shapes are holograms, not literal structures suspended in the blood, since anything that solid floating in someone's bloodstream would kill them instantly. He ties the phenomenon to water's capacity to hold and express imprinted information, the same mechanism behind Veda Austin's frozen water photography."},{"title":"Parasites Are Not the Enemy","body":"Jacob rejects the idea that parasites cause disease, arguing worms show up specifically where heavy metals and unprocessed waste have accumulated, eating garbage rather than creating it. He walks through the shaky foundational research behind malaria, where early scientists could not even agree whether the specimens they were calling parasites were parasites or ordinary red blood cells, and describes the medical field's own admitted category of pseudo parasites: dust, pollen, and platelets routinely misidentified under a microscope. He extends this to the popular claim that cancer itself is a parasite, arguing tumors simply attract worms the way a garbage pile attracts flies."},{"title":"Cancer as the Body's Final Attempt to Heal","body":"Working from a homotoxicology framework, Jacob describes disease as a six phase progression from simple excretion and inflammation through deposition, impregnation, degeneration, and finally the de-differentiation phase the body calls cancer, each phase a deeper stage of the same stagnation. His approach for a cancer patient centers on elimination diets, saunas, sweating, and emotional release rather than suppression, because reversing the terrain reverses the cancer. He compares suppressing symptoms with medication to duct taping an overflowing septic tank: the waste doesn't disappear, it just backs up until the whole system fails, manifesting later as a worse chronic illness."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text":"They figured out a way to blame gay people for this disease.","author":"Jacob Diaz","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/455381a0-d166-44e4-8795-115770962281/JACOB-DIAZ.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"The funny thing about the antibody test for HIV is that there's 70 conditions that you can get a positive test for HIV.","author":"Jacob Diaz","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/455381a0-d166-44e4-8795-115770962281/JACOB-DIAZ.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"If you don't have the terrain conducive to AIDS, you're not gonna develop AIDS.","author":"Jacob Diaz","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/455381a0-d166-44e4-8795-115770962281/JACOB-DIAZ.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"I would never get a vaccine. fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "It's a one-way street when converting out of the belief that invisible boogeymen are making you sick and there's nothing about your own behaviors that could stop it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It always made sense to me that as a religious person, a loving God would not create these tiny pathogens that are designed to kill you.", "author": "Jacob Diaz", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/455381a0-d166-44e4-8795-115770962281/JACOB-DIAZ.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Every single day we are on this earth breathing, we have huge amounts of streptococcus bacteria in our throat at all times.
